> 馬，蹄可以踐霜雪，毛可以御風寒，齕草飲水，翹足而陸，此馬之真性也。

Hooves that tread frost and snow, hair that holds off wind and cold, grazing, drinking, lifting a leg to gallop — this is a horse's true nature.

The paragraph is careful in a way that is easy to miss. All four pieces of evidence are bodily, and none of them has anything to do with spirit. 莊子 is not arguing from mysticism. He is arguing from hooves.

## 真性

性: 心 with 生 as phonetic — what birth carries. 真性 is the original, before manufacture.

## 雒, and the four cuts

雒 reads 烙 — branding with fire. It sits in a series: 燒之 (burn the hair), 剔之 (cut the mane), 刻之 (pare the hoof), 雒之 (brand the hide).

Four operations, each deeper than the last. By the fourth, the mark is permanent and it is in the skin.

## 皁棧: moving the horse indoors

皁 is a manger; 棧 is the plank flooring of a stable. Together: the whole apparatus of confinement — the horse moved from open ground into a built space.

The order of伯樂's work is worth noting: the cutting comes before the confinement, and the confinement teaches what the cutting could not.

## The horse did not become bad. It learned.

馬知介倪、闉扼、鷙曼、詭銜、竊轡 — the horse learns to lean against the shaft, to jerk the collar, to strike the canopy, to spit the bit, to work the reins loose.

None of these exist on the open plain, and none is needed. They are produced by pressure.

This is the chapter's sharpest line, and it is a diagnosis of every training program ever run: the pressure you apply is not digested, it is learned. Press a thing and it learns what to defend. When it has learned the whole set, you are no longer holding a compliant horse. You are holding an opponent who knows your harness.

馬之知而態至盜者，伯樂之罪也 — if the horse's knowledge reaches the level of theft, that is 伯樂's fault.

## 天放 is defined, not praised

一而不黨，命曰天放 — one, without partisanship: that is 天放.

天 is the natural; 放 is not indulgence, it is being without a rope.

The definition has two conditions, and both are required: 一, no ranking of high and low; 不黨, no grouping for mutual protection. Keep only "放" and drop "一" and you get license, which is the other error 莊子 refuses.

## 素樸: undyed silk, unhewn wood

素 is raw silk before dyeing; 樸 is timber before cutting. Both words mean "not yet processed."

That is the chapter's scale. Judge a society not by how rich or how orderly it is, but by how much of it has not been processed.

## 蹩躠, 踶跂: the characters themselves strain

Both describe standing on tiptoe, propping yourself up. 莊子 uses these two shapes to describe the posture of 仁義: not flowing out from the heart, but held up on a frame.

The glyphs make the point before the sentence does: this is effort.

## 同德 is not uniformity

同其所得 — each getting what it needs, and all of them having enough. Weave and wear, plough and eat, each doing their own work, no comparison of rank.

That is what 同 means here — and it is the opposite of the later "unify the thinking" sense of the word.

## The test

Name one person or group you are currently training, correcting, or improving. Then find the 皁棧 — the confinement you built — and ask what they have learned inside it. Not what you taught. What they learned to defend.
